title: Метод работы с актёрами  (A Method for Working with Actors)

segments.t: Greeting the director with theatrical charm, Nagiyev welcomes her to Claude Monet as if it were her first visit. She surprises him by revealing she has been coming to the restaurant for two weeks straight to observe him in real life before casting her film.
Ничего себе, вы просто так хорошо выглядите.
Перестал узнавать.
Ну и значит.
Виктория Сергеевна.
Добро пожаловать.
Благодарю вас.
А я смотрю, вы не в первый раз.
Я хожу уже к вам две недели.
Вот какая, чего же я не знаю.
Такой мой метод работы с актёрами.
Я хотела посмотреть, какой вы в жизни.
Гениально, вот гениально.
Да, вот что там, да.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
Ничего себе, вы просто так хорошо выглядите.
'My goodness, you look simply wonderful.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'nothing' and finishing on 'look'. Vika answers right away.
Перестал узнавать.
'I hardly recognized you at first.' The meaning hinges on 'to stop' working together with 'to recognise' in spoken Russian.
Ну и значит.
'Well, that means.' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'so' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Виктория Сергеевна.
'Viktoriya Sergeyevna.' Vika anchors the line on 'Viktoriya', while 'Sergeyevna' completes the thought. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Добро пожаловать.
'Welcome to our restaurant.' In Russian, the idea of 'good' flows naturally into 'to welcome' without extra filler words.
Благодарю вас.
'Thank you very much.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'to thank' and 'you' in a few short words.
А я смотрю, вы не в первый раз.
'And I see this is not your first time here.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'and' and 'I' in a few short words. Vika answers right away.
Я хожу уже к вам две недели.
'I have been coming to your place for two weeks already.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'weeks' without extra filler words.
Вот какая, чего же я не знаю.
'Is that so, how did I not know about it?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'there you go' before landing on 'know'.
Такой мой метод работы с актёрами.
'That is my personal method of working with actors.' The meaning hinges on 'such' working together with 'actor' in spoken Russian. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Я хотела посмотреть, какой вы в жизни.
'I wanted to see what you are like in real life.' Notice how Russian expresses 'I' and 'life' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Гениально, вот гениально.
'Brilliant, simply brilliant.' Vika anchors the line on 'brilliant', while 'there you go' completes the thought.
Да, вот что там, да.

'Yes, well, let us see what is over there.' In Russian, the idea of 'yes' flows naturally into 'there' without extra filler words. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
